- Technical Division operates one of the country's largest installations of Coating and Lamination Capacity
- Integrated presence across spinning, speciality fabric processing, technical textiles and garmenting
- Established supplier of high value-added military products to the Government of India, Ministry of Defence and the Indian Army, including Extreme Cold Weather Clothing Systems, OBRNe defence items and Carrying Gear
- Contract manufacturing relationships with global backpack brands
- Captive wind power - 55 wind mills of 13.195 MW in Tamil Nadu whose entire generation is consumed captively at the spinning unit, supplemented by associate L K Distributors Private Ltd whose wind generation is fully consumed by the Company
- Continuous replacement of inefficient spindles with state-of-the-art machinery to reduce operational cost and improve output quality
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Availability of quality cotton — Management names availability of quality cotton as an identifiable risk and concern for the textile industry that may have a severe impact on the Company's operating and financial performance; the spinning business is cotton-based.
- Erratic cotton price movement and raw material cost fluctuation — Listed both as a risk and concern in the MD&A and as a threat; management is relying on further supportive government measures to soften the price of cotton and other raw materials, i.e. the mitigation is outside the Company's control.
- High cost of power and other inputs — Flagged as an identifiable risk for the industry; the Company mitigates part of it by consuming the entire output of its 13.195 MW wind mills captively at the spinning unit, but the balance of power and input cost remains exposed.
- Availability of skilled labour — Named by management among the identifiable risks and concerns for the textile industry, relevant to a spinning, processing and garmenting operation.
- Structural shift to Man Made Fibre — Listed as a threat in the MD&A; the Company is historically a cotton yarn spinner predominantly in the hosiery segment, so a demand shift away from cotton is a structural mix risk.
- Geopolitical disruption and supply-chain stress — Management states the US-Iran war has severely affected the business environment in India, bringing spiralling oil prices, supply-chain issues and a glut-like situation.
- Dependence on government policy support — The MD&A frames the industry's long term sustainable future as subject to the extension of supportive measures by the appropriate governments and availability of a favourable business climate, and the optimistic outlook rests on Government initiatives such as the Union Budget 2026-27 textile programme and Mega Textile Parks.
- Concentration in Government defence orders — Stated near-term visibility rests on large Ministry of Defence / Department of Military Affairs orders for Extreme Cold Weather Clothing System suits (15,000 sets to be supplied before June 2026 and 24,585 sets during FY2026-27), making order flow from a single government customer a structural dependency.
- Negligible export presence in yarn — During the year exports accounted for a negligible share of the spinning unit's yarn sales, leaving the yarn business dependent on domestic demand.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: The Company is historically involved in the manufacturing of cotton yarn, predominantly in the Hosiery Segment in medium counts and is slowly shifting focus towards finer yarn counts, with an operational capacity of 52,416 spindles near Coimbatore. Its Technical Division houses one of the country's largest installations of Coating and Lamination Capacity, producing B2B and B2C products for home textile, digital imaging, baby and adult mattress protection, defence, medical and allied customer categories, while the Processing factory at SIPCOT, Perundurai makes speciality fabrics for premium customers. The Garments Division manufactures high value-added military products, particularly OBRNe defence items, Cold weather clothing systems and Carrying Gear, and also does contract manufacturing of backpacks for global brands.
business.title: What they do

business.body:
- **Spinning:** Cotton yarn (Hosiery Segment, medium counts, shifting towards finer counts), Waste cotton (sold indigenously)
- **Technical Division:** Coated and laminated B2B and B2C products
- **Processing:** Nylon and Polyester knits, Pile fabrics, Microfiber fabrics made of conjugate yarn, Free cut and seamless products
- **Garments Division:** OBRNe defence products, Cold weather clothing systems (Extreme Cold Weather Clothing System suits), Carrying Gear, Contract-manufactured backpacks for global brands
- **Wind Power:** Wind electricity consumed captively

outlook.body:
- Shift the cotton yarn focus from medium counts in the Hosiery Segment slowly towards finer yarn counts
- Build on the Technical Division's coating and lamination installation to serve B2B and B2C categories - home textile, digital imaging, baby and adult mattress protection, defence, medical and allied customers
- Serve premium customers through speciality fabrics (nylon and polyester knits, pile, microfiber conjugate-yarn and free cut / seamless products) from the SIPCOT, Perundurai processing factory
- Focus the Garments Division on high value-added military products - OBRNe defence, cold weather clothing systems and carrying gear - alongside contract manufacturing of backpacks for global brands
- Consume wind power captively from the Company's 55 wind mills in Tamil Nadu to contain power cost
- The routed governance sections set out no explicit dividend-payout or capital-allocation policy. Form AOC-1 records that the Company has no subsidiaries (Part A: not applicable), with L K Distributors Private Limited held as a 26% associate whose wind power output supports the Company's own operations. The Notice of the 45th Annual General Meeting places declaration of dividend on equity shares before members as ordinary business, and proposes special resolutions to alter the Object Clause of the Memorandum of Association - inserting a new main object covering interior design materials, wall design papers and decoratives, textile materials, technical textiles and customised products for military, defence, air force and marine users, and activities in artificial intelligence, robotics, nano-technology and R&D - and to adopt a new set of Articles of Association under the Companies Act, 2013, indicating an intent to widen the permitted scope of reinvestment into technical textiles, defence products and advanced technology. Form AOC-2 records that there were no material contracts or arrangements or transactions with related parties during the year under review, and none not at arm's length.
- Captive renewable power: 55 wind mills located in the State of Tamil Nadu with an installed capacity of 13.195 MW, the entire power generated being utilised captively at the spinning unit
- Associate L K Distributors Private Ltd is engaged in wind power generation and its entire generation during the year was consumed by Shiva Texyarn Ltd, extending the Company's renewable sourcing
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: The annual report describes no new greenfield project or announced capex programme. The existing footprint is a spinning unit near Coimbatore with an operational capacity of 52,416 spindles (unchanged during the year under review), the Technical Division housing one of the country's largest installations of Coating and Lamination Capacity, a processing factory at SIPCOT, Perundurai making speciality fabrics, a Garments Division making high value-added military products, and 55 wind mills in Tamil Nadu with an installed capacity of 13.195 MW whose entire output is consumed captively at the spinning unit. Expansion is incremental and modernisation-led: management states it is continuously engaged in identifying inefficient spindles and replacing them with state-of-the-art technology machinery to reduce high operational cost and get better quality of output, and the Company is continuously putting efforts to widen the product mix under the Technical Textile segment while starting to concentrate on manufacture of finer counts of yarn. Growth in the near term is order-led rather than capacity-led: the Company has secured significant Ministry of Defence orders, with 15,000 sets of Extreme Cold Weather Clothing System (Suit) to be supplied before June 2026 and a further order for 24,585 sets from the Department of Military Affairs, Indian Army to be supplied during financial year 2026-27. The Directors' Report records no material changes and commitments affecting the financial position of the Company during the period under review and no change in the capital structure. Captive renewable supply is supplemented by associate L K Distributors Private Ltd, engaged in wind power generation, whose output was fully consumed by Shiva Texyarn Ltd.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- The Indian textile industry is fast growing and has a long term sustainable future, subject to the extension of supportive measures by the appropriate governments and availability of a favourable business climate
- Union Budget 2026-27 has carved out a Five-Part Integrated Programme covering the entire textile value chain, i.e. from fibre to fashion
- Union Budget 2026-27 provides for establishment of Mega Textile Parks focusing on scaling up manufacturing and value addition, particularly in technical textiles
- Considering the Government's various initiatives in support of the Indian Textile Industry, the outlook continues to be an optimistic one
- Management expects more and more supportive measures from the appropriate Governments to soften the price of cotton and other raw materials
- Headwind: raw material cost fluctuations and erratic price movement of cotton
- Headwind: the US-Iran war has severely affected the business environment in India - spiralling oil prices, supply-chain issues and a glut-like situation
- Headwind: structural shift to Man Made Fibre
